questions.q: 'El verano pasado, yo ___ a México con mi familia.' The regular preterite of viajar in the yo form is:
options: viajé
viajó
viajo
viajaba
questions.explanation: -Ar verbs take -é in the yo preterite, with a written accent: viajé. 'Viajo' without the accent is the present 'I travel.'

questions.q: Which set of endings is correct for regular -er and -ir verbs in the preterite?
options: -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -ieron — the same set for both
-é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -aron
-er verbs use -í, -iste, -ió; -ir verbs use -é, -aste, -ó
-ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían
questions.explanation: -Er and -ir verbs share one set of preterite endings, so comer and salir end the same way: comió / salió, comimos / salimos, comieron / salieron.

questions.q: 'Viajo' and 'viajó' are different words. 'Mi hermano viajó a Oaxaca' means:
options: my brother traveled to Oaxaca (one finished past trip)
my brother travels to Oaxaca (every year)
my brother is traveling to Oaxaca right now
my brother will travel to Oaxaca
questions.explanation: The accent on -ó marks the third-person preterite. Without it, 'viaja' would be the present. In the preterite the accent carries the tense.

questions.q: 'alojarse' (to stay / to lodge) is reflexive. 'We stayed in a small house near downtown' is:
options: Nos alojamos en una casa pequeña cerca del centro
Me alojé en una casa pequeña cerca del centro
Se alojaron en una casa pequeña cerca del centro
Nos alojan en una casa pequeña cerca del centro
questions.explanation: Nosotros takes the pronoun 'nos' and the regular -ar preterite ending -amos: nos alojamos. (It also happens to match the present-tense nosotros — context tells you it is past here.)

questions.q: 'Recorrimos el centro histórico a pie' means:
options: We traveled around / toured the historic center on foot
We visited one museum in the historic center
We looked for the historic center on a map
We lived in the historic center
questions.explanation: Recorrer is to move through or around a place, covering ground — not just visiting a single spot.

questions.q: In a trip narrative, 'el recuerdo' can mean a memory or ___, and 'el itinerario' is ___:
options: a souvenir  /  the day-by-day plan of the trip
a photograph  /  the return flight
a postcard  /  the hotel bill
a guidebook  /  the passport
questions.explanation: Spanish uses 'recuerdo' for both the memory and the object that holds it. An itinerario is the trip laid out in time, stop by stop.
